entries.proposition: A one-patient clinical note: compound heterozygous PARKIN variants, early-onset parkinsonism and glioblastoma.
entries.snippet: This report describes such a patient with compound heterozygous mutations in PARKIN, early-onset parkinsonism, and GBM.

entries.proposition: PARKIN is described as a 1.3 Mb gene containing the fragile site FRA6E between exons 2 and 8.
entries.snippet: PARKIN is one of the largest genes in the human genome (1.3 Mb) and contains a chromosomal fragile site (CFS) FRA6E (6q26) between exons 2 and 8.

entries.proposition: The authors themselves note that the two phenotypes rarely co-occur.
entries.snippet: it is surprising that PARKIN mutations rarely result in both parkinsonism and GBM

entries.proposition: Case: carrier of two causative variants, one a small deletion and one an exon duplication; two younger brothers carry the same compound heterozygous state, with no statement of their tumour status.
entries.snippet: Two of his younger brothers were also compound heterozygous

entries.proposition: Autopsy: infiltrating glioblastoma in the temporal lobe, severe nigral cell loss, no Lewy bodies.
entries.snippet: no Lewy bodies or Alzheimer pathology

entries.proposition: The inference to a predisposition rests on rarity of the combination in one individual.
entries.snippet: Given the rarity of PARKIN mutations and GBM, their concomitant occurrence in a single individual may well be more than a coincidence.

entries.proposition: Proposed mechanism: reduced PARKIN ligase function raises cyclin E, a mitotic-instability route in dividing cells; the tumour was not genotyped and no second hit is shown.
entries.snippet: Mutations in PARKIN show decreased PARKIN E3 ligase function with resultant accumulation of cyclin E, creating the potential for mitotic instability in dividing cells.

entries.proposition: The authors say larger studies are needed and cite epidemiology pointing the other way (lower cancer risk in neurodegenerative disease).
entries.snippet: Future clinical genetic studies are needed to determine whether there is indeed an increased risk for development of malignancies in PARKIN carriers.

entries.proposition: The figure is a two-box hypothesis schematic (one-hit familial parkinsonism versus a two-hit cancer predisposition model with a second-hit mutation); it plots no data and the 'second hit' is a placeholder.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1: top, 1-hit hypothesis arrow from germ-line PARKIN mutations on both alleles to nigrostriatal degeneration and parkinsonism; bottom, 2-hit hypothesis with germ-line PARKIN mutations on both alleles or on one allele, and a 2nd hit mutation box, to growth advantage and development of cancer.
